{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ne-o","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f9b8d7083d382517f94a7baea13f123f0a6d953ca9e221a0ce0436ea9d6cd2ba","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ne-class-o:lineage:58","source_registry_sha256":"66161d94cc863d3cf353417f54f101bf8681de71fc4c3b73f43c86f2be1c7398","source_liveness_sha256":"78587b1f8f8617c7b8b0a43b3f0679698b900b7d64ddfc387c1773ac070571e8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Passing interactions, turns, parking and rail crossings","heading":"Passing interactions, turns, parking and rail crossings","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Passing interactions, turns, parking and rail crossings

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A65
The handbook prohibits double parking beside an already stopped or parked vehicle. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A65
Do not park or stop on a sidewalk, in an intersection or on a crosswalk. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A65
The printed no-parking-or-stopping distance is thirty feet from a roadside flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign or other traffic-control device. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A65
The printed parking restriction extends twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A65
The manual prohibits parking or stopping on a bridge, in a highway tunnel or within fifty feet of railroad tracks. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A65
Do not block a public or private driveway or ignore signs prohibiting standing, stopping or parking. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A65
The printed fire-hydrant parking clearance is fifteen feet. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A65
When parking uphill beside a curb, set the parking brake and turn the wheels away from that curb. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A65
For other hill-parking situations, turn the wheels toward the curb or roadway edge. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A65
Accessible spaces are reserved at all hours for properly plated or permitted vehicles from which the person with the qualifying disability enters or exits. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A65
Do not park in the access aisle beside an accessible parking stall. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A65
The printed accessible-parking fine maxima are one hundred fifty dollars for a first offense, three hundred for a second and five hundred for a third. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A65
Blocking a curb cut or wheelchair ramp can result in an accessibility-ramp violation ticket. [A65]
Source: [A65 -> pdf-0065]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A66
Rail crossings may have a round advance sign, crossbuck, white X or RR pavement text, a no-passing marking or a stop line. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A66
Approach railroad tracks at a controlled speed that allows a stop if necessary; always expect rail traffic. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A66
Stop for an approaching-train signal, lowered gate, flagman's warning or a crossing stop sign. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A66
A visible train or audible train whistle requires a stop when crossing would be hazardous. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A66
Stop at the railroad stop line; without one, stop between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest rail. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A66
Never drive through, around or beneath a railroad gate or barrier. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A66
After stopping, check every track and confirm there is enough room for the entire car beyond the rails. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A66
Expect buses and hazardous-material trucks to stop at railroad crossings. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A66
Do not shift gears while traversing tracks, and watch for additional trains or on-track equipment. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A66
If a vehicle stalls on a crossing, get everyone out of the vehicle and off the tracks immediately. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A66
After evacuation, the manual directs use of the crossing sign's emergency number when no train is visible, to try to stop rail traffic. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A66
Keep clear of the tracks if rail traffic is approaching; the emergency instructions also direct a call to nine-one-one. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A66
An ENS sign is typically blue and provides a continuously available railroad-dispatch emergency contact at or near the crossing or crossbuck. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A66
Railroad dispatchers answering the ENS number can attempt to stop trains at the crossing during an emergency. [A66]
Source: [A66 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A67
The DOT number below an ENS dispatch number identifies the precise crossing being reported. [A67] [A66]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A67
ENS reports can describe malfunctioning warning equipment, disabled vehicles blocking tracks, trespassers or other unsafe crossing conditions. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A67
Use added caution at rail crossings because trains and other on-track equipment cannot stop quickly. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A67
Never race a train or other on-track equipment across the tracks. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A67
Avoid gear changes on railroad tracks because a stalled vehicle can be left in danger. [A67]
Source: [A67 -> pdf-0067]
